user_input: My CGPA has tanked to 6.2 because I've spent the last three months overanalyzing every single WhatsApp status she posts and trying to bump into her near the library. Yesterday, I finally confessed my feelings to her over a voice note, and all she replied was 'Aww, that's sweet, but I only see you as a study buddy.' I have my midterms starting Monday and I can't even read a single line of my OS textbook without bursting into tears; my parents are already asking why my internal marks are so low.
sandhi_response: Rejection hurts with a physical intensity that makes focusing on anything else, especially demanding exams, feel almost impossible. Let yourself grieve this quiet loss, and try to take just one small, gentle step toward your books without expecting yourself to be perfectly okay right now.

user_input: Everyone in my batch is getting placed, and my inbox is filled with Congratulatory emails while I'm sitting here with two active backlogs and a broken heart. The guy I've loved since our freshman year induction just announced on LinkedIn that he's relocating to Bangalore with his long-distance girlfriend. I didn't even know he had a girlfriend; I feel so incredibly stupid and invisible, like a ghost watching everyone else move forward with their lives while I'm stuck in this dark, dusty hostel room.
sandhi_response: It is incredibly heavy to feel left behind in every aspect of your life while watching someone you quietly loved build a future without you. Right now, your pain is valid, and it is okay if you don't have the strength to celebrate others while you are still trying to rebuild your own pieces.

user_input: We had our final year project evaluation today and he didn't even look at me when the external examiner was asking questions, even though we spent weeks working on this model together. I thought working on this project would bring us closer, but he's already planning his MS in the US and I'm just a temporary stepping stone he used to clear the final semester hurdle. I'm dreading the graduation ceremony because I know he'll hug everyone else, but I'll just get a formal handshake and then he'll disappear forever.
sandhi_response: The realization that someone you hoped to be close with is preparing to drift away can leave a cold, heavy ache in your chest. It is completely natural to feel hurt by this distance, so please treat yourself with immense kindness as you navigate this painful transition.

user_input: I’ve spent the last three weeks sitting next to her in the DSA coding lab, helping her debug her trees and graphs while my own head is spinning. Today she casually mentioned her boyfriend just got placed at Microsoft and how they are planning a trip to celebrate. My compiler threw another error, and I just stared at the screen trying not to let my tears drop on the keyboard because my CGPA is a pathetic 6.8 and I'm clearly not even in her league, academically or otherwise. I feel like a ghost in my own life, coding her dreams while mine are dead on arrival.
sandhi_response: It is incredibly heavy to carry the quiet ache of loving someone up close while feeling like your own life and achievements are shrinking in their shadow. Please know that your worth is not defined by a coding compilation or a placement tier, and it is completely okay to gently step back to protect your own heart right now.

user_input: We were supposed to be studying for the end-sem exams in the library, but he spent the whole time texting someone else, smiling at his screen while completely ignoring my explanations of the syllabus. My dad keeps calling me about my mock test scores, warning me that if I don't get my act together I'll end up with backlogs and no job. I sat there pretending to highlight my notes, but my chest felt so tight because I'm failing my exams and I'm completely invisible to the one person I can't stop thinking about. I feel so incredibly stupid for caring this much about someone who wouldn't even notice if I stopped showing up to group studies.
sandhi_response: It is deeply exhausting to try and anchor someone else's attention while your own world feels like it is slipping under academic pressure. Take a slow breath right now, let your shoulders drop, and remember that you deserve to direct that care back toward your own healing.

user_input: She posted her placement offer on the class WhatsApp group, and everyone is spamming congratulations. I gathered all my courage and sent her a long, genuine text congratulating her privately, hoping maybe she'd see how much I care. She left me on read but replied to group threads instantly, and now my mom is calling me asking why my placement prep is so slow compared to others. I am sitting in my room with the lights off, watching my phone screen light up with updates, feeling this deep, hollow ache that I am simply not good enough to be loved or even acknowledged.
sandhi_response: Seeing the silence on your screen when you have offered your genuine warmth is a very sharp, isolating kind of pain. You are allowed to mute those notifications for tonight and simply exist without having to prove your value to anyone else.

user_input: I stayed up for three nights straight pulling all-nighters to finish our major project evaluation because I wanted him to see me as reliable, hoping he'd finally realize how much I do for him. Today, during the evaluation, he gave all the credit to another guy in our group just to look cool, and didn't even mention my name. I had to sit there through the entire viva, smiling while the professor praised them, feeling utterly disposable. I spent my whole month's energy trying to buy his affection with my labor, and I've ended up exhausted, hurt, and still completely unloved.
sandhi_response: It hurts deeply when you pour your energy and care into someone, only to find your effort treated as invisible. Your dedication and intelligence are highly valuable, and you do not have to over-extend yourself to earn the space or respect you already deserve.

user_input: I saw them at the campus fest tonight holding hands with someone from the senior batch who already has a 12 LPA package locked in. Here I am with two active backlogs, struggling to find a basic internship, standing in the corner of the lawn alone. The contrast is so loud it makes me want to scream; I’m failing my career, I'm failing my parents, and the person I love doesn't even know I exist. I feel like an absolute loser who is destined to watch everyone else get their happy endings while I drown in my own failures.
sandhi_response: Watching someone you care for move forward while you feel anchored down by backlogs and career worries is a heavy weight to carry. Let yourself grieve this moment without using it as proof that you are failing, because your path is still unfolding and your own pace is entirely valid.

user_input: I spent the entire night debugging our group project code just so she'd notice me during the lab evaluation tomorrow. But during the viva, she didn't even look my way—she was busy texting this senior who already bagged a 15 LPA placement at Oracle. My CGPA is sitting at a miserable 6.8, I've got two pending backlogs, and my parents are calling every Sunday asking why I can't be more like my cousin. sandhi_response: It is incredibly painful to pour your heart and energy into being seen, only to feel like your worth is being measured against someone else's achievements. Please know that your value is not a calculation of your CGPA or your placement status, and you deserve to exist without constantly having to prove your worth.

user_input: Every day in the library, I sit two tables away from him, pretending to solve mock tests while my chest literally aches. Today he asked me for my DSA notes, and I stayed up till 3 AM making them perfect, but today he didn't even sit near me—he was laughing with some guy who cleared the Google kickstart rounds. I feel like such an idiot, sacrificing my own sleep and prep for someone who views me as a free resource. I can't focus on my gate exam prep anymore; my mind is just a loop of how unwanted I am.
sandhi_response: Exhausting yourself to earn a crumb of attention is a heavy burden to carry, especially when you are already under so much pressure to perform. It is completely okay to step back and protect your own energy, because your kindness should never come at the cost of your own peace.

user_input: I got rejected in the second round of campus placements today, and to make it worse, I opened WhatsApp and saw her status with a guy from the CS branch at a cafe. My heart dropped; I couldn't breathe, and my hands started shaking while my dad was lecturing me on the phone about our family's financial situation. It feels like everyone is moving forward, getting placed, finding love, and I'm just this broken, unlovable burden stuck in my room with a pile of uncompleted assignments. Why am I never enough for anything or anyone?
sandhi_response: That moment when academic pressure, family expectations, and personal heartbreak collide can feel entirely suffocating. I hear how overwhelmed you are, and it is completely valid to grieve these heavy losses without needing to fix everything all at once.

user_input: She got the highest package in the class during the day-zero placements, and she didn't even reply to my congratulatory text, though she's actively posting on Instagram. user_input: During the placement prep group discussions today, he didn't even look at me when I spoke, but he kept praising this other girl's strategy. My roommate is talking about his own girlfriend and placement offers, and here I am, unable to write a single line of Python code for tomorrow's lab because I'm paralyzed by how lonely I feel. I feel like I'm failing at both my career and my personal life, and there's no escape.
sandhi_response: That physical heaviness in your chest and stomach is your body's way of carrying a massive amount of unspoken grief and exhaustion. Let's put the coding lab and the pressure aside for just a moment; you deserve to rest and breathe without grading yourself on your loneliness.

sandhi_response: It is incredibly draining to pour your energy into someone who only sees you when they need help, especially while you're carrying the heavy weight of placements and exams. It makes complete sense that you feel exhausted and unseen right now, but please know that your worth isn't defined by how much of yourself you have to give away to be noticed.

user_input: My mock test results came out today and I scored in the bottom 10% because I couldn't focus for even ten minutes. sandhi_response: Seeing the person you care about choose someone else, especially when you are already struggling with academic pressure and family expectations, feels like a deep, personal failure. Your pain is completely real, but please remember that your academic standing and your capacity to be loved are not tied to anyone else's choices or achievements.

user_input: The placement coordinator posted the final list on WhatsApp, and she got placed in Bangalore while I'm stuck trying to clear my papers here.
